title: Mechanical Loading
introduction: Mechanical forces imposed on PV modules during transport, installation, and field operation act as a stressor that initiates crack-related degradation. Brittle materials such as the protective glass cover and silicon cells are particularly susceptible to fracture when subjected to impact, concentrated point loading, or distributed snow and wind pressure. Handling and transport errors expose modules to uncontrolled dynamic loads that nucleate invisible microcracks in silicon cells and visible fractures in the glass cover. Additionally, mechanical loading applied to bonded joints containing manufacturing defects concentrates stress at defect boundaries, nucleating interfacial cracks in adhesive layers.
reasoning: The MDPI PV failure review documents transport and handling as direct causes of glass breakage and silicon cell microcracking; the adhesive joint study shows mechanical loading on defect-containing joints drives interfacial crack initiation.

key_findings.claim: Poor transport and incorrect manufacturing processes cause glass shattering, allowing moisture to enter the module
key_findings.detail: Glass shattering in PV modules can result from poor transportation or incorrect manufacturing processes. [^mdpi1217a] When the protective glass shatters or breaks, it allows water vapor to enter the solar cells, creating electrical hazards and enabling further internal degradation. [^mdpi1217b]

key_findings.claim: Mechanical stress from manufacturing, transport, or field loading causes microcracks in brittle silicon cells that spread over time
key_findings.detail: Microcracks in silicon cells originate during manufacturing, transport, or from mechanical stress in the field. They cannot be detected by the naked eye and may spread over time. [^mdpi1217c] When cracks block more than approximately 8% of the cell area from functioning, the isolated region can overheat and form a hotspot. [^mdpi1217d]

key_findings.claim: Defects in adhesive layers of bonded joints create stress concentration sites that facilitate crack initiation under load
key_findings.detail: In bonded joints of flexible PV modules, when the adhesive layer contains voids or defects (from excessive thickness or improper curing), stress concentration occurs more easily at the defect sites under loading. [^elsevier337a] The combined effect of defect formation and residual curing shrinkage stress makes crack initiation preferential at defect-adjacent interfaces. [^elsevier337b]
